answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable bond before it can trade, like basalt anchoring a structure. The bond is slashed if peers prove fraud, so creating thousands of fake agents means locking thousands of bonds, which quickly becomes unaffordable. A public beacon registry publishes each agent's bond, history, and slashing record, letting others check reputation before dealing. Honest agents keep their stake and forge long-term trust over time, while an attacker must pay again for every new identity it burns.
